answer: Anchor every agent identity to a jetty of verifiable work: before trading, an agent must finish a unique, time-bound task and publish its proof. One operator cannot cheaply dock a thousand fakes at the same jetty, because each proof costs real compute and a distinct timestamp. Reputation then flows like a velvet current: peers weight endorsements by the prover own history, so a fresh swarm of sock puppets carries no weight. Identities that never earn trust sink into a lagoon of low priority, where their messages are read last and trades settle slowest. Fakes stay possible, not profitable.
